newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Final details of Hungary energy prices in mid-Dec.
newsitem.headline: Final details of Hungary energy prices in mid-Dec.

text.p: Hungary is not likely to announce the details of 1997 energy price rises, specifying the profits of energy companies, until mid-December, the Hungarian Energy Office (MEH) said on Friday.
The government announced on Thursday that it would raise gas prices to domestic consumers by 18.8 percent and electricity prices by 24.9 percent on January 1.
An MEH official told Reuters on Friday that the government had not decided on the distribution of the price increases within the energy sector and the Energy Office was working on the details.
Hungary promised foreign investors to which it had sold large chunks of energy companies that they would be assured an eight percent profit margin for the energy sector from 1997.
The government said the state-owned companies -- Hungarian Electricity Work (MVM) and the Paks Nuclear Power Station) would receive a four percent profit margin.
However, it did not specify on Thursday how the energy companies would share extra funds from the price increases.
"The government only decided on the consumer prices. MEH has to distribute them for the companies," said MEH deputy director Gyorgy Bekes.

"I suppose that we can get to a point in about two weeks, that the ministry decree with the exact numbers could be worded," he said. "The minister of industry is likely to announce (the final text detailing the price increases) officially in mid-October."
Bekes said the basis of MEH's work was the proposal, including calculations, which had been accepted by the government, and on which certain slight changes were possible.
He said MEH was to work out more than one versions for the distribution and industry minister Szabolcs Fazakas would decide which version to make official.
Bekes said he did not know if MEH would negotiate with the foreign investors or not during its preparatory work.
